rw: FBLA, Future Business Leaders of America, is a student organization built for high schoolers, offering business competitions, networking and career learning that directly teach about business careers.

ww.A cooking club only: A cooking club focuses on food preparation skills and recipes, so it would not teach students about business careers, finance, management or marketing in any organized way.
ww.A chess tournament only: A chess tournament tests strategy and concentration in a game setting, but it offers no instruction or networking about business careers, so it does not meet the stated goal.
ww.A fantasy sports league: A fantasy sports league is a recreational game about picking athletes, and it does not give students structured exposure to business careers, mentors or professional skills training.

rw: A labor market is where workers offer their labor and employers seek workers, and the interaction of both sides there determines employment levels and the wages paid for jobs.

ww.A bank: A bank is a financial institution that holds deposits and makes loans, so it is not the market where workers and employers meet to trade labor.
ww.A store that sells tools: A store that sells tools is a retail business selling goods, which is a product market, not the place where workers offer labor to employers.
ww.A tax office: A tax office collects and processes taxes for the government, so it is an agency, not the market where workers and employers come together to exchange labor for pay.

rw: When few workers supply a rare skill while employers demand it strongly, scarcity pushes employers to compete for those workers by offering higher wages, which is basic supply and demand.

ww.Skills have no value: Skills have real value because employers pay for what skilled workers can do, so saying they have none is false and cannot explain why those wages are higher.
ww.The government sets wages: Wages are mostly set by supply, demand and bargaining in the labor market, not by the government, apart from minimum wage laws, so this does not explain rare-skill pay.
ww.Employers dislike skilled workers, and s: Employers generally value skilled workers because they produce more, which is why they pay them more, so claiming employers dislike them and pay less reverses the actual pattern.

rw: Employability is the mix of skills and personal traits, such as reliability, communication and knowledge, that make a person attractive to employers and likely to be hired and keep a job.

ww.The number of jobs available in the econ: Counting the jobs available in the economy describes job openings or employment data, not a person's own qualities, while employability is about how hireable one individual is.
ww.The salary a person earns: Salary is the pay a person earns after being hired, which is an outcome of work, whereas employability describes the skills and traits that make someone hireable beforehand.
ww.The size of a company: The size of a company describes an employer's headcount or scale, not a worker's qualities, so it has nothing to do with whether a person is hireable.

rw: A gig job is short-term or task-based work, such as ride driving or delivery, and it is often arranged through an app that matches workers with individual tasks.

ww.A government post: A government post is a public sector position that is usually stable and long term, which is the opposite of the short, task-based nature of gig work.
ww.A volunteer role with no pay at a charit: A volunteer role with no pay is unpaid service, but a gig job is paid work, so this description fails the basic idea that gigs earn income.
ww.A permanent salaried role: A permanent salaried role offers ongoing employment with a regular paycheck, which is the reverse of a gig job that is temporary and paid by the task.

rw: A benefit package is non-wage compensation, such as health insurance, paid leave and retirement contributions, that employers provide on top of pay and that adds real value to a job.

ww.The hourly wage a worker earns for each: An hourly wage is only the base pay for time worked, while a benefit package covers other compensation, so this describes wages and not benefits like insurance.
ww.A loan: A loan is borrowed money that must be repaid, which is a financial product and not a part of what an employer provides as compensation.
ww.A tax: A tax is a required payment to the government that is taken from earnings, so it is a deduction and not a package of benefits given to workers.

rw: Overtime pay is the extra pay, often time-and-a-half, that a worker gets for hours beyond a standard limit such as 40 hours in a week, as many labor laws require.

ww.A bonus for arriving early at work, whic: Arriving early is not what triggers overtime, which depends on hours worked beyond the standard limit, so a bonus for early arrival describes something else entirely.
ww.Pay for vacation: Pay for vacation is paid time off, which rewards no extra hours, whereas overtime pay is earned by working more than the standard number of hours.
ww.A tax: A tax is money withheld for the government, while overtime is extra earnings for extra hours, so a tax cannot be the meaning of overtime pay.

rw: The first 40 hours pay 40 x 12 = $480, and the 4 overtime hours pay 4 x 18 = $72 at time-and-a-half, so the total is 480 + 72 = $552.

ww.$528, found by paying all hours at the r: Paying all 44 hours at the regular rate gives 44 x 12 = $528, but that ignores the time-and-a-half premium owed for the 4 hours beyond 40.
ww.$576, found by paying all hours at time-: Paying all 44 hours at time-and-a-half would be 44 x 18 = $792, not $576, and only the hours beyond 40 get the premium rate.
ww.$480, found by paying only 40 hours: Paying only 40 hours gives 40 x 12 = $480, but she also worked 4 overtime hours that earn 4 x 18 = $72 more, so the total is higher.

rw: A payroll deduction is an amount subtracted from gross pay, such as income tax, Social Security or insurance premiums, which leaves the smaller net pay that the worker actually receives.

ww.A bonus: A bonus is extra money added to pay, so it increases earnings, whereas a payroll deduction is an amount subtracted from gross pay before the worker is paid.
ww.A raise: A raise increases a worker's pay rate, so it adds to earnings, while a payroll deduction takes money out of gross pay, making these opposite in effect.
ww.A gift: A gift is something given without payment, and it is not a systematic subtraction from a paycheck, so it does not describe what a payroll deduction is.

rw: A pay stub is a statement from the employer showing gross pay, hours worked, deductions and net pay for one pay period, which lets workers verify what they were paid.

ww.A bank statement: A bank statement lists account deposits and withdrawals from the bank, not the employer's breakdown of hours, pay and deductions for a pay period, so it is a different document.
ww.A tax form for the year: A tax form for the year, such as a W-2, summarizes annual earnings and taxes, whereas a pay stub covers a single pay period with hours and deductions.
ww.A job application: A job application is what a person submits to apply for work before being hired, so it has no information about pay, hours or deductions from a paycheck.

rw: Reviewing each pay stub lets workers check hours, pay rate and deductions for errors, so mistakes such as missing overtime or wrong withholding can be found and corrected quickly.

ww.To impress the boss: Impressing the boss is not the purpose of checking a pay stub, which exists to protect the worker's own money by catching mistakes in what was paid.
ww.To pay more tax: Reviewing a stub does not make anyone pay more tax, because taxes are set by law and withholding, and checking only confirms the amounts are correct.
ww.To avoid keeping records of earnings, si: Workers should keep records of earnings and compare them with stubs, and relying on the employer's copy would leave them unable to prove errors, so avoiding records is poor advice.

rw: An elevator pitch is a short summary of who you are and what you offer, delivered in about 30 seconds so that a listener quickly understands your value as a candidate.

ww.A job application: A job application is a written form submitted to an employer, whereas an elevator pitch is a brief spoken introduction of yourself, so these are different tools.
ww.A speech given in an elevator only: An elevator pitch is not limited to elevators, because it can be used at networking events or fairs, and the name refers to its brevity, not its location.
ww.A long report presented to investors ove: A long report to investors over several hours is the opposite of an elevator pitch, which must be brief, personal and focused on a job seeker's strengths.

rw: A career counselor helps people explore careers, match their interests and abilities to jobs, and plan the education and job steps needed to reach their career goals.

ww.Hires employees for a firm, after readin: Hiring employees is the job of an employer or recruiter, while a career counselor works with people to explore careers, so this describes a different role.
ww.Pays wages: Paying wages is the duty of an employer or payroll department, and a career counselor does not pay anyone, because the job is to advise people on careers.
ww.Sets taxes: Setting taxes is done by governments and legislatures, and it has nothing to do with the advising work of a career counselor, who guides people on career choices.

rw: An applicant tracking system is software that employers use to collect, organize and screen job applications, often filtering resumes by keywords before a human recruiter reads them.

ww.A tool that trains staff: Training staff is done through training programs and instructors, not through an ATS, which is software that handles applications and not employee development.
ww.A tool that tracks employees' hours and: Tracking employee hours and attendance is the work of a timekeeping or payroll system, while an ATS tracks job applicants during hiring, before they are employees.
ww.A tool that pays wages: Paying wages is a payroll function, and an ATS is a hiring tool that manages applicants, so it does not issue pay to anyone.

rw: Including keywords from the posting helps a resume pass automated screening software and shows a recruiter that your skills match what the employer asked for in the job.

ww.To make the resume longer so that it fil: Making a resume longer to fill the page is a poor reason, because employers prefer concise resumes, and keywords are chosen for relevance and not for length.
ww.To hide experience: Keywords are meant to show your experience clearly and not hide it, so using them does the opposite of concealing what you have done.
ww.To confuse the employer: The aim of keywords is to communicate clearly with the employer and show a match, so trying to confuse the employer would hurt the application instead of helping it.

rw: A good approach is to name a real weakness and explain how you are improving, which shows honesty, self-awareness and a willingness to grow, qualities employers value.

ww.Name a weakness that makes you unfit for: Naming a weakness that makes you unfit for the job is honest but self-defeating, because it gives the interviewer a reason to reject you, and a better answer shows improvement.
ww.Say you have no weaknesses: Saying you have no weaknesses sounds unrealistic and lacks self-awareness, so interviewers may doubt your honesty, which makes this a weak answer.
ww.Refuse to answer: Refusing to answer looks evasive and unprepared, and it gives the interviewer nothing to evaluate, so it is a poor way to handle a common question.

rw: Two weeks is the typical notice period when resigning, giving the employer time to arrange a replacement and hand over duties while keeping a good professional reputation and references.

ww.Two years: Two years is far too long for a notice period, because standard practice is a short notice of a couple of weeks, so it does not match what employers expect.
ww.Two minutes: Two minutes is not a real notice period, since it gives the employer no time to plan, and a professional resignation gives much more warning than that.
ww.None ever: Giving no notice ever is not standard, because professional practice is to give notice so the employer can plan, and leaving abruptly can harm your reputation and references.

rw: The best answer shows you know the company and explains how your skills fit, which proves you did your research and links what you offer to what they need.

ww.I don't know: Saying I do not know shows no interest or preparation, so it fails to give the interviewer any reason to think you want this particular job.
ww.I have no other options, so I am applyin: Saying you have no other options and will apply anywhere makes you sound desperate and uninterested in this company, so it gives the interviewer no reason to hire you.
ww.I need money: Saying I need money may be true, but it shows no interest in the company or the role, and so it does not persuade the interviewer to hire you.
